## CEO overview

- **What is changing:** When a task's recorded Herdr workspace no longer exists, relaunch now recovers by opening a fresh workspace in the same work location instead of failing permanently.
- **Why it matters:** Workspace cleanup or server restarts previously left tasks stuck because relaunch could not resume without the old workspace.
- **Customer or business impact:** Operators can relaunch Herdr-backed tasks reliably after workspace changes, with updated session metadata and a clear fallback record when replacement succeeds.
- **Risk and rollout:** The fallback is narrow: it refuses ambiguous workspace inspection, never allocates a new work copy or changes the branch, defers fallback status until replacement fully succeeds, and restores prior metadata when replacement fails. Behavioral stub coverage exercises success and rollback paths.

## What changed technically

- Extended `fm-spawn --relaunch` for Herdr to inspect recorded workspace presence after the worktree isolation proof: recreate only the task tab when the workspace still exists, or run the normal fresh-endpoint path when it is dead, publishing fresh session metadata and a status fallback line without allocating a new worktree; ambiguous workspace inspection refuses.
- Updated relaunch documentation in agent-control and herdr-backend docs describing endpoint adoption versus recreation.
- Added stubbed Herdr backend tests covering workspace fallback, metadata updates, status logging, and prior-record rollback when replacement fails.

## Validation

- **Checks passed:** Live Herdr lab validation for three primary scenarios (missing-workspace fallback, fallback status after create succeeds, no new worktree on dead workspace); behavioral stub tests for fallback success and failed-create rollback; full relaunch suite including new Herdr cases; prior pipeline intent, rebase, review, test, document, lint, and push steps completed on head 8efcc0c3e7f22dac1abed677bc64cb2025526874.
- **Checks not run:** Create-failure rollback, ambiguous duplicate-workspace refusal, and stub regression scenarios were validated through behavioral backend stubs rather than repeated live Herdr runs in this cycle.
- **Evidence and limitations:** Live transcripts and stub test output are captured under the branch evidence directory. Stub tests prove orchestration and metadata behavior; live validation exercised the primary operator path against a real Herdr server in an isolated lab session.

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Operator relaunches a Herdr-backed task whose recorded workspace was removed; replacement uses a fresh Herdr endpoint in the same worktree and updates session/workspace/tab/pane metadata | pass | live | herdr-relaunch-fallback-live.log |
| Successful workspace fallback writes a status line naming the old and new workspace ids only after create_task succeeds | pass | live | herdr-relaunch-fallback-live.log |
| Relaunch does not allocate a new worktree when the Herdr workspace is dead | pass | live | herdr-relaunch-fallback-live.log |
| When Herdr workspace replacement fails during create, prior durable metadata is restored and rollback is recorded | untested | no | stub test test_herdr_relaunch_failure_restores_the_prior_record |
| When workspace presence inspection is ambiguous (duplicate ids), relaunch refuses with an inspection error instead of proceeding | untested | no | stub script herdr-relaunch-ambiguous-stub.log |
| Behavioral backend-stub regression: missing-workspace fallback publishes replacement metadata and records fallback in status | untested | no | stub test test_herdr_relaunch_falls_back_when_recorded_workspace_is_missing |

## Module-boundary decision

Current module retained: Herdr relaunch fallback extends the existing spawn relaunch and control paths; workspace inspection, metadata publication, and rollback remain in their existing producer-owned modules. No new control plane or worktree allocation path was introduced.

## Decision needed

No decision required.
